'''''Lightsaber Techniques Painting''''' was a [[Painting/Legends|painting]] available in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] sometime after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a conflict between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="SWG" /> The painting depicted the seven<ref name="Card-SWGTCG-Lightsaber Techniques Painting">{{SWGTCG|set=The Shadow Syndicate|cardname=Lightsaber Techniques Painting}}</ref> [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] [[Lightsaber combat/Legends#Individual Fighting Forms|combat forms]]&mdash;[[Form I/Legends|Shii-Cho]], [[Form II/Legends|Makashi]], [[Form III/Legends|Soresu]], [[Form IV/Legends|Ataru]], [[Form V/Legends|Shien / Djem So]], [[Form VI/Legends|Niman]], and [[Form VII/Legends|Juyo / Vaapad]]<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' {{C|Pages 19-21}}</ref>&mdash;used by members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="SWG" />

==Behind the scenes==
''Lightsaber Techniques Painting'' is a painting that appeared in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|MMORPG]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]''. It was obtained by redeeming a "loot card" from the ''[[Star Wars Galaxies Trading Card Game]]'' expansion set ''[[The Shadow Syndicate]]''. The loot card was only obtainable during a limited time event known as the "Booster Shot scenario" which ran from [[November 11]] to [[December 15]], [[2009]]. Players received the loot card after their first completion of the scenario, in which they had to face [[Booster Terrik]]. After obtaining the card, the players could redeem it and then claim it on one of their characters on the same SWG account to receive the actual painting, which could be used as housing decoration. Because [[Form VII/Legends|Form VII]] is depicted in both "Juyo" and "Vaapad" variants, the painting actually depicts eight lightsaber combat stances, not seven. While it would appear that the Aurebesh lettering along the top and left are meant to spell out "The Seven Forms of Lightsaber Combat" and "Jedi Techniques," many of the letters used are incorrect.
